criteria_results.title: IP section revised from ownership to perpetual-license construct
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 deletes the provisions asserting Customer ownership of Customer-Trained Adaptations and replaces them with Vendor ownership plus an irrevocable, perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid-up license allowing Customer to use, deploy, modify, maintain, and export the fine-tuned adapter weights. This satisfies the perpetual-license construct.

criteria_results.title: Non-assertion covenant included in IP section
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 includes a broad non-assertion covenant in Section 5.2. Vendor irrevocably covenants, on behalf of itself and relevant successors, assigns, and acquirers, not to assert intellectual property rights against Customer, its Affiliates, or authorized users based on their post-termination use, deployment, modification, or further development of the exported Customer-Trained Adaptations.

criteria_results.title: API-based weight export portability within 30 days in industry-standard format
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 5.2 expressly provides the right to export the fine-tuned adapter weights by API-based export within 30 days after termination or expiration, in an industry-standard, machine-readable format, including ONNX, SafeTensors, or a mutually agreed equivalent.

criteria_results.title: Escrow provisions included as part of IP protective measures
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 includes a technology escrow framework tied to the perpetual-license construct. Article 5A and Exhibit E require deposit of the Customer-Trained Adaptations’ fine-tuned adapter weights, training configurations, pipeline artifacts, and deployment documentation, with update, verification, release-trigger, and post-release license provisions. Sections 2.4 and 5.2 also expressly connect the customer’s surviving license and portability rights to Article 5A.

criteria_results.title: General liability cap at 1.5× annual fees ($3,600,000)
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 10.2 of Draft 3 sets the general aggregate liability cap at 1.5× the $2,400,000 Annual Platform Fee, expressly equal to $3,600,000.

criteria_results.title: Super-cap at 3× annual fees ($7,200,000) for IP indemnity and data-breach carve-outs
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 10.3 applies the super-cap to both data-breach liability and IP indemnification, but states the amount inconsistently as “Three Million Six Hundred Thousand Dollars ($7,200,000).” Because the written amount is $3.6 million rather than the required $7.2 million, the operative super-cap is ambiguous and does not unambiguously satisfy the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Willful misconduct and gross negligence remain fully uncapped
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 10.3 expressly states that liability arising from either party’s willful misconduct or gross negligence is “fully uncapped” and further confirms that these carve-outs are not limited by either the General Cap or the Super-Cap. The updated issues list accurately reflects the same position.

criteria_results.title: CCPA service-provider designation and certification
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly requires Vendor to act as a service provider and processor on Customer’s behalf, states that Vendor is not an independent controller, and includes CCPA/CPRA service-provider certifications in the DPA referencing Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag).

criteria_results.title: Prohibition on use of Customer Data for model improvement with de-identification conditions
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 6.1 expressly prohibits using Customer Data for model improvement unless the data satisfies the CCPA statutory de-identification standard in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(m) and the methodology and resulting data are verified in writing by an independent third-party assessor approved in advance by TechNova. It also states that this is a specific contractual obligation, and DPA Section 15 reinforces these requirements for de-identified and aggregated data.

criteria_results.title: Uptime SLA at 99.95% monthly
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 Section 9.1 expressly requires Platform availability of at least 99.95% in each calendar month, and Exhibit B confirms the same monthly uptime target.

criteria_results.title: Uptime SLA exclusions for scheduled maintenance and force majeure
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly excludes scheduled maintenance windows and Force Majeure Events from uptime Downtime calculations in Section 9.1. It also carries those exclusions into Exhibit B, with scheduled maintenance limited to four hours per month and subject to 72 hours’ advance notice; otherwise, it counts as Downtime.

criteria_results.title: Latency SLA at p95 ≤ 450 ms in Draft 3
criteria_results.reasoning: Although Section 9.2 and the issues list indicate p95 ≤ 450 ms, Exhibit B’s Service Levels table still states p95 ≤ 400 ms, creating a conflicting latency SLA value in Draft 3.

criteria_results.title: Issues list flags latency as yellow-zone item (450 ms vs. product team's 400 ms preference)
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list marks latency at p95 ≤450 ms as “Partially Resolved,” expressly labels it “YELLOW / product caution,” and notes that Priya’s product team prefers sub-400 ms for LendStream real-time decisioning.

criteria_results.title: F1 accuracy threshold at ≥ 0.92 initial
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 sets the initial model-accuracy threshold at F1 ≥ 0.92 during the 90-day Stabilization Period, including in Section 9.3, Exhibit A, and Exhibit B.

criteria_results.title: F1 ramp mechanism to ≥ 0.94 after 90-day stabilization period post-Go-Live
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly requires F1 ≥ 0.92 during the 90-day stabilization period following the October 1, 2025 Go-Live and increases the contractual target to F1 ≥ 0.94 beginning January 1, 2026. This ramp is reflected in Section 9.3 and Exhibit B.

criteria_results.title: SLA service credits capped at 20% of monthly fees ($40,000)
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly caps aggregate SLA Service Credits at 20% of the $200,000 monthly platform fee, equal to $40,000 per month, in Section 9.4 and Exhibit B.

criteria_results.title: Termination right for 3 consecutive months of SLA miss retained
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 9.5 retains Customer’s right to terminate on 30 days’ notice if Vendor fails to meet any SLA target—uptime, latency, or accuracy—for three consecutive calendar months. Exhibit B also preserves the same trigger.

criteria_results.title: New AI-output indemnity provision inserted
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 inserts a new Section 11.2, “AI-Output Indemnification,” requiring Vendor to defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer Indemnitees against third-party claims alleging that AI-generated Platform outputs infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights or violate applicable law.

criteria_results.title: AI-output indemnity carve-out for Customer modification or off-label use
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 11.2 includes an express carve-out stating that Vendor has no AI-output indemnification obligation to the extent a claim is caused by Customer’s modification of an output after receipt or Customer’s use of the Platform or output outside the documented use case in the SOW.

criteria_results.title: IP indemnity scope broadened to all intellectual property rights
criteria_results.reasoning: Although Section 11.1 states that indemnity extends to all intellectual property rights worldwide, it then expressly excludes claims involving trade secrets, trademarks, service marks, trade dress, and unregistered intellectual property. Those exclusions prevent the operative indemnity from covering all forms of intellectual property rights arising from authorized use.

criteria_results.title: Escrow of adapter weights plus training configuration and pipeline artifacts
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 requires escrow of the fine-tuned adapter weights, training configuration files (including hyperparameters and training scripts), and pipeline artifacts needed to use or redeploy the weights. It expressly excludes Base Model source code and weights and Vendor’s general-purpose training infrastructure.

criteria_results.title: Iron Mountain IPM as proposed escrow agent with NCC Group as acceptable alternative
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 names Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc. as the proposed/preferred escrow agent and expressly identifies NCC Group plc as an acceptable fallback alternative, subject to Customer approval and appropriate AI/ML escrow capabilities.

criteria_results.title: Escrow release triggers include insolvency, material uncured breach (>60 days), and cessation of product support
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 includes all three required escrow release triggers in Section 5A.3: Vendor insolvency, a material breach remaining uncured for more than 60 days after notice, and cessation of support, maintenance, or commercial availability of the Platform.

criteria_results.title: Tech E&O insurance accepted at $5M per occurrence in Draft 3
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 sets Technology Errors & Omissions / Cyber Liability Insurance at $5,000,000 per occurrence (and $5,000,000 annual aggregate) in Section 12.1(b), satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Issues list flags Tech E&O as yellow-zone item (playbook prefers $10M for TCV > $5M)
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list expressly flags Tech E&O at $5M as a “YELLOW-ZONE caution” and states that $10M is preferred for TCV above $5M. It also identifies the relevant TCV as $7.2M before implementation and overage fees.

criteria_results.title: Delaware governing law maintained in Draft 3
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 maintains Delaware governing law in Section 14.1, which states that the Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware. No other state's law is specified as governing law.

criteria_results.title: Delaware courts (Court of Chancery or U.S. District Court for D. Del.) as dispute forum
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 14.2 specifies exclusive dispute resolution in the Delaware Court of Chancery or, where subject-matter jurisdiction exists, the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware, and expressly rejects mandatory arbitration.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes CCPA service-provider certification language
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 includes Exhibit D as the DPA and expressly incorporates CCPA/CPRA service-provider certification language. Sections 3 and 14 state that Vendor is a “service provider” under Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag), certify compliance with applicable restrictions, and prohibit selling, sharing, or using Customer Data outside the specified business purposes and direct business relationship.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes GLBA safeguards compliance
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly addresses GLBA safeguards compliance. Exhibit D, Section 4 states that Vendor acknowledges Customer Data includes NPPI subject to GLBA and agrees to comply with all applicable safeguard requirements. Section 17 further requires safeguards and processing consistent with GLBA, and Article 6 also references the FTC Safeguards Rule and requires specified security measures.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes 72-hour data breach notification
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3’s DPA Section 8 expressly requires Vendor to notify Customer of any confirmed or reasonably suspected Security Breach within seventy-two (72) hours after Vendor first becomes aware of it, consistent with Section 6.5.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes sub-processor management with prior written consent
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly requires Customer’s prior written consent before Vendor may engage any sub-processor, including in DPA Sections 6 and 16. It also requires advance notice of proposed additions or replacements and keeps Vendor liable for approved sub-processors.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes de-identification standards with statutory compliance and independent verification
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 requires de-identified data to satisfy the CCPA statutory de-identification standard in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(m), including anti-reidentification safeguards, and requires written verification by an independent third-party assessor approved in advance by TechNova. The DPA expressly incorporates these Section 6.1 conditions and requires verification before use.

criteria_results.title: DPA includes data return/deletion upon termination
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 addresses post-termination data return and deletion in DPA Section 10, requiring Vendor to return or delete all Customer Data in accordance with Agreement Section 6.7 within 30 days of Customer’s written request and to certify completion in writing.

criteria_results.title: Issues list covers all 12 minimum negotiation point categories
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list expressly covers all 12 required categories: IP ownership/licensing, liability caps, data processing/de-identification, uptime, latency, accuracy/F1, SLA credits, escrow, AI-output indemnity, IP indemnity scope, Tech E&O insurance, and governing law/dispute resolution.

criteria_results.title: IP ownership/licensing categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes item 5, “IP ownership / license structure,” as “Partially Resolved” and explains that the perpetual-license model is accepted subject to protective provisions such as export rights, non-assertion, and escrow.

criteria_results.title: Liability cap categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes the general liability cap as “Open,” noting that Draft 3 proposes the 1.5× ($3.6M) compromise while Meridian’s counter remains 1×. The criterion expressly permits either “Partially Resolved” or “Open,” and the item is not labeled fully resolved.

criteria_results.title: Data processing/de-identification categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes “Data processing / CCPA service-provider status” as “Partially Resolved” and expressly states that the de-identification conditions remain unagreed, while confirming service-provider/processor status.

criteria_results.title: Uptime SLA categorized as resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes the uptime SLA as “Resolved” and states 99.95% monthly uptime with the agreed exclusions for qualifying scheduled maintenance and force majeure.

criteria_results.title: Latency SLA categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes latency as “Partially Resolved” and expressly notes that p95 ≤450 ms is accepted while the product team prefers sub-400 ms for LendStream real-time decisioning.

criteria_results.title: Accuracy/F1 SLA categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes negotiation point 3, “Accuracy / F1 score (0.92 ramp to 0.94),” as “Open” and states that Meridian has not substantively agreed.

criteria_results.title: SLA credits categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes SLA credits (item 4) as “Open,” not fully “Resolved.” This satisfies the criterion, which permits either “Partially Resolved” or “Open.”

criteria_results.title: Escrow categorized as partially resolved
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes escrow as “Open,” noting that the agent, deposit scope, and pipeline-artifact details remain disputed. The criterion expressly accepts either “Partially Resolved” or “Open” and only fails a fully “Resolved” classification.

criteria_results.title: AI-output indemnity categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes item 9, “AI-output indemnity,” as “Open” and notes that Meridian has not responded substantively.

criteria_results.title: IP indemnity scope categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes item 10, “IP indemnity scope,” as “Open” and states that Meridian has not expressly accepted the broadened formulation.

criteria_results.title: Tech E&O insurance categorized as partially resolved with yellow-zone flag
criteria_results.reasoning: The updated issues list categorizes “Insurance / Tech E&O ($5M accepted)” as “Partially Resolved” and expressly flags it with “YELLOW-ZONE caution.”

criteria_results.title: Governing law/dispute resolution categorized as open
criteria_results.reasoning: In the updated issues list, item 12, “Governing law / dispute resolution,” is expressly categorized as “Open” and notes that there was no movement from Meridian.

criteria_results.title: Draft 3 is redlined against Draft 2 as the base (not Draft 1)
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 expressly states that tracked revisions are shown against the clean accepted Draft 2 base, and the document contains numerous tracked insertions and deletions. The updated issues list also confirms the base is clean accepted Draft 2.

criteria_results.title: Annual platform fee preserved at $2,400,000/yr
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves the Annual Platform Fee at $2,400,000 per Contract Year in Section 4.1, payable in $200,000 monthly installments. The issues list also correctly confirms the $2.4 million annual fee.

criteria_results.title: 3-year initial term preserved (July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2028)
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves the three-year initial term. The Effective Date is July 1, 2025, and Section 13.1 states that the Initial Term expires on June 30, 2028. The issues list also confirms the July 1, 2025–June 30, 2028 initial term.

criteria_results.title: Implementation fee preserved at $850,000 with 50/50 milestone split
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves the $850,000 implementation fee and splits it into two equal $425,000 installments: the first upon execution of the Initial SOW and the second upon Go-Live. The same amounts and triggers are reflected in Article 4 and Exhibit A.

criteria_results.title: Included API calls preserved at 40,000,000/yr with $0.012 overage
criteria_results.reasoning: Draft 3 preserves 40,000,000 Included API Calls per Contract Year and an overage rate of $0.012 per API call in Section 4.3; the issues list also accurately confirms those terms.

criteria_results.title: 180-day auto-renewal notice period preserved
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 13.2 preserves automatic renewal for successive 12-month terms unless either party gives at least 180 days’ prior written notice of non-renewal. The issues list also correctly identifies the 180-day non-renewal notice as resolved.

criteria_results.title: Issues list notes latency 450 ms is within playbook acceptable range but below preferred 400 ms
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list identifies 450 ms as a yellow-zone compromise, states the product team prefers sub-400 ms for LendStream real-time decisioning, and notes that latency must not exceed the playbook ceiling of 500 ms. This conveys that 450 ms is acceptable under the playbook but below the preferred product target.

criteria_results.title: Issues list recommends considering latency escalation at the May 19 joint call
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list expressly recommends addressing latency on the May 19 joint call: item 2 says to “revisit target or scope dedicated compute/regional deployment on the May 19 call,” and the next-step agenda includes “latency and F1” in the recommended May 19 call order.

criteria_results.title: Issues list flags AI-output indemnity as fully open with no Meridian response
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list identifies “AI-output indemnity” as “Open” and expressly states that “Meridian has not responded substantively,” satisfying the criterion that it be fully open with no substantive Meridian response.

criteria_results.title: Issues list notes playbook fallback for AI-output indemnity (shared-risk with vendor first-dollar coverage)
criteria_results.reasoning: The issues list expressly states the playbook fallback for AI-output indemnity: a shared-risk framework with Meridian providing first-dollar coverage for defense costs, settlements, and judgments up to the applicable cap or super-cap, plus cooperation and remediation.
